plate_findings.evidence: Caption: “Low-power view shows a diffuse population of monomorphic lymphoid cells with a starry sky appearance.”
Caption describes a diffuse population of monomorphic lymphoid cells.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Human H&E histopathology from a representative case of Burkitt lymphoma showing the classic diffuse monomorphic-cell infiltrate and starry-sky pattern. B: Human high-power H&E image of representative Burkitt lymphoma showing characteristic intermediate-sized monomorphic neoplastic lymphoid cells. Mitotic figures and apoptotic bodies are captioned but are not in the allowed findings vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Anagnostopoulos et al. Burkitt Lymphoma-A Guide to Biological Features, Diagnosis and Differential Diagnosis.. Cancers 2026. doi:10.3390/cancers18040579. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Representative morphology and immunophenotype of BL. (A) Low-power view shows a diffuse population of monomorphic lymphoid cells with a starry sky appearance. (B) High-power view highlights neoplastic cells that are of intermediate size comparable to the histiocytes. They exhibit round central nuclei harboring several small and distinct nucleoli surrounded by a small rim of cytoplasm. Mitotic figures and apoptotic bodies are present. Immunohistochemical analysis shows that the lymphoma cells express CD20 (C), CD10 (D), BCL6 (E) and MYC (F). Ki67 demonstrates a high proliferation rate, close to 100% (G). In cases associated with an EBV infection, all neoplastic cells are positive for EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) (H). BCL2 is not expressed by the neoplastic cells (I), while IRF4/MUM1 can be expressed with low intensity (J).
in_text_mentions: itotic figures, as well as a high number of apoptotic bodies [126]. A “starry sky” pattern is usually present, resulting from the interspersed tingible body macrophages. Extensive necrosis is common. The histologic features of a typical BL case are shown in Figure 2. In bone marrow trephines, the neoplastic cells can be present with either a nodular or diffuse growth pattern and may not show the starry sky pattern, particularly in cases with less extensive infiltrates. A representative case of BL with bone marrow involvement is shown in Figure 3. Box 1 summarizes the diagnostic features of BL.

plate_findings.evidence: Caption identifies a gross 6 cm firm mass at the ileo-cecal junction; the specimen is labeled proximal ileal margin, distal cecal margin, and appendix.
Caption states that the lymphoma is composed of sheets of monotonous lymphocytes invading the bowel mucosa.
Caption explicitly identifies the characteristic starry-sky appearance caused by scattered histiocytes engulfing apoptotic lymphoma cells.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Gross patient pathology from the 10-year-old's ileocecal resection directly demonstrates the Burkitt lymphoma mass described in the caption. b: Low-power H&E image shows a diffuse lymphoid infiltrate invading bowel mucosa, directly supporting the panel-specific caption diagnosis of Burkitt lymphoma. c: Higher-power H&E section demonstrates the classic starry-sky pattern and monotonous lymphoid proliferation explicitly attributed to Burkitt lymphoma.

Intussusception leading to bowel obstruction is a well-documented complication of bowel involvement and reason for emergent presentation, particularly in the pediatric population (Figs. 2 and 3) [29]. On ultrasound, signs of intussusception include concentric alternating echogenic and hypoechoic bands of bowel layers (“target sign”) on transverse views and corresponding “pseudokidney” sign on longitudinal views.
